scope: One pair of miter leaves and their closed wicket flaps. Equal-level opening and closing only. Does not simulate the filling of an entire lock.
gaps: Original gate dimensions and exact date unknown. Scope is a dimensioned modern demonstration.
No original gate built by Leonardo survives with that provenance.
Holder image licence terms were not obtained. The image URL is a digital-edition surrogate.

date.note: Watermark study dates about 1499. Milan museum favours about 1506.

scale_m.note: Conservative swept envelope x -2.3 to 2.3, y 0 to 2.7, z -0.35 to 2.85.

assumptions.statement: All numerical procedural dimensions, positions, angles and chosen material classes in parts and joints are modern modelling assumptions. They do not measure Leonardo’s sheet or any museum replica.
assumptions.reason: The sheet does not dimension a complete assembly.

assumptions.statement: Every numerical physics input explicitly tagged C is an illustrative modern assumption, not a historical measurement.

joints.notes: Joint values add to the listed rest orientation. The pivot is the heel post's axis in the quoin post's frame; the heel post turns on its pintle and in its collar. Fixed children inherit motion.

input_rate.note: Maximum leaf speed for this 24 second hand-operated cycle

drive.justification: Both gate hinges are manual inputs. Water levels are already equal. No geared drive.

motion.visitor_12s: In twelve seconds the two leaves open halfway through a 76 degree movement. The wicket flaps stay closed. t is phase-local seconds. Angles are radians.

animation_notes: Do not animate a mechanism missing from the evidence.
Opening under a head difference is prohibited. No rapid water-level equalisation is implied.
The manual cycle is reversible because a person can open and close the leaves. No mechanical energy is regenerated.

The leaf's root is the round heel post, turning about its own axis on an iron pintle in a socket and in an iron collar at its head. Motion replaces only the additional hinge angle. Do not count rest angles twice.
No gearing exists in this scope. The small doors stay shut on their latches and the filling of the lock is outside the illustrated operation.

[museum, gates] The 1953 interpretive model and surviving repaired gates are separate objects. Our dimensions and equal-level motion are new assumptions, with no replica geometry reused.

[folio] The sheet draws each leaf as a frame of a heel post, a mitre post, four rails and one long brace, planked on its far face, the heel held by an iron collar and strap, a small door with strap hinges and a drop latch worked by a rod from the top, rings on the mitre posts and a paved floor. [geometry] Every size, the pintle and socket, the hollow quoin, the mitre sill, the pegs and nails are the museum's reconstruction of how such a gate was built.

dimensions.leonardo_wording: Qui sta la catena colla quale si serra il portello col saliscendo.
dimensions.note: [folio] This locates the latch chain, not a measurement. No numerical gate dimension or Richter number verified. No braccio conversion is required.

claims.tested_by_leonardo: No direct test record established in the inspected sources.
claims.built_in_lifetime: [museum] The San Marco lock was real. Bartolomeo Della Valle built the linking locks. The catalogue explicitly allows either an improvement or a survey by Leonardo. [gates] Preserved gate timber spans the sixteenth to nineteenth centuries.
later_tests: [gates] Museum material investigations in 2016 examined the historic gate components. This is conservation evidence, not a controlled test of a Leonardo prototype.

physics.formula: For a vertical leaf, F = rho*g*b*(h_high^2-h_low^2)/2. The hydrostatic load acts normal to each leaf.

inputs.note: Assumed water density used in the hydrostatic pressure calculation.
Modern model leaf width measured in the plane of one gate leaf.
Assumed water depth on the higher-water side, measured above the common sill.
Assumed water depth on the lower-water side, measured above the same sill.

physics.result: F = 1000*9.81*2.06155*(4-1)/2 = 30,336 N, about 30 kN per leaf. At equal 2 m depths F_net = 0 N. This omits seal friction and hinge friction.
physics.limitations: This arithmetic is a conditional illustration, not an experimental result.
physics.verdict_en: An assumed one metre level difference loads each leaf with about 30 kN. Equalising the levels removes that pressure difference.
physics.verdict_de: Ein angenommener Höhenunterschied von einem Meter belastet jeden Torflügel mit etwa 30 kN. Gleiche Wasserstände beseitigen den Druckunterschied.

myths.correction: [museum] Do not assign the invention of canal locks or the entire Naviglio to Leonardo. The record leaves his specific contribution open.

research.confidence: High for folio and ambiguity of attribution. Medium for date. Modern illustrative geometry only.
